prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a parking lot collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1037; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents our client in connection with a collision that occurred in a parking lot and resulted in personal injuries to our client. Please direct all future communications regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, letter, or in person. If your insured or any representative of your company has already been in contact with our client, please let us know so that we can address it.

We ask that you provide the bodily injury liability limits of the policy issued to your insured, along with a certified copy of the declarations page and any excess or umbrella coverage that may apply. Please also confirm the name of the adjuster assigned to this claim.

Finally, we demand that your company preserve all evidence relating to this incident. This includes photographs, dash camera or surveillance footage, vehicle data, witness statements, recorded calls, claim notes, and any repair or appraisal records. Destruction or alteration of such material could seriously prejudice our client's claim. We look forward to your prompt written response.
